subject: Atlas Payments POC - success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Atlas Payments POC - success criteria & next steps

Hi Elena -

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call to make sure we’re aligned before the POC kickoff. TL;DR: we propose a 2-week trial with success criteria around latency, throughput, cost/token, and quality.

POC objective
- Validate Redwood inference for Atlas Payments’ customer-facing fraud scoring and payment classification use cases.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (initial):
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 250ms (single-request, 99% of traffic profile)
- Throughput: sustained ~50 requests/sec for peak evaluation windows (burst to 150rps)
- Cost: average cost/token < $0.0005 (target for production economics)
- Quality: classification accuracy / intent match >= 90% on labeled evaluation set; false-positive rate <= X (we'll refine once we get sample labels)

Trial plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): share POC plan & network requirements (attached).
- Week 1: ingest sample dataset, run baseline tests (latency/throughput/cost) against our verified model variant.
- Week 2: iterate on prompt/quantization/configs; run evaluation on your labeled set; handoff results & recommendation.

Owners & roles
- Redwood: Jordan (sales lead) - overall coordination; Rafael (SE) - performance tuning & infra; Marissa (CS) - onboarding & runbooks.
- Atlas: Elena - product lead; Victor - infra/SRE contact (network/VPC config).

Immediate asks for Atlas
- Confirm that the success criteria above look right or suggest edits.
- Send a representative labeled evaluation sample (CSV) and any rate/traffic profile details.
- Confirm Victor’s email for network/VPC setup.

I’ve attached a one-page POC plan and network topology sketch for your infra team. If that looks good I’ll share a calendar invite for a kickoff Friday morning (PT).

Thanks - talk soon.

-
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>

Subject: Re: Atlas Payments POC - success criteria & next steps

Thanks Jordan - great summary, and appreciate the clear owners. A few notes from our side after syncing internally: 

Success criteria adjustments
- Latency: p95 target 200-250ms is fine; for production we’d prefer p95 <= 200ms but for the POC 250ms is acceptable.
- Throughput: baseline traffic is ~30rps, with spike to 120rps during peak windows; 50rps sustained is a fine test target.
- Cost: the $0.0005/token target looks reasonable - we’ll want to see effective cost once you include batching & prefix caching.
- Quality: we’ll validate on our labeled payment classification set - target 90% top-1; we’ll also measure precision on high-cost false positives.

Data & access
- I’ll share a redacted sample CSV (2000 rows) by EOD.
- Victor (cc'd) will coordinate network requirements - Victor, can you confirm the contact who owns firewall/VPC peering?

Timeline
- 2-week trial is fine. Kickoff Friday morning PT works for us; proposed window 9:00-10:00am PT.

One question: we will need SOC2 and data handling details for our security team before we transmit sample data. Can you push the SOC2 and relevant compliance artifacts to the drive link?

Thanks -
Elena
Head of Product, Atlas Payments
elena@atlas-payments.com
